title: PacBio SMRTbell Library Preparation 3.0 Manual
author: Jae Hee Jang
materials: Quick-spin RM1 in a microcentrifuge to collect liquid
Proceed to the next step of the protocol
Quick-spin RM2 in a microcentrifuge to collect liquid
Quick-spin the tube strip in a microcentrifuge
Quick-spin RM3 in a microcentrifuge to collect liquid
Optionally input Barcode information for each sample

steps.title: Prepare Reaction Mix (RM1)
steps.instruction: In a new microcentrifuge tube combine Repair buffer (8 µL per library), End‑Repair mix (4 µL per library) and DNA‑Repair mix (2 µL per library) for a total of 14 µL per library; increase the total volume by 10 % for pipetting error (or by 25 % if preparing eight or more libraries).

steps.title: Add Barcoded Adapters (if needed)
steps.instruction: If barcoding samples, add 4 µL of the appropriate barcoded adapter from the SMRTbell Barcoded Adapter Plate 3.0 to each sample and omit the SMRTbell adapter in the later ligation step.

steps.title: Add RM1 to Samples and Mix
steps.instruction: Add 14 µL of the prepared RM1 to each sample (bringing the total reaction volume to 60 µL), pipette‑mix using wide‑bore tips, then quick‑spin the tube strip in a microcentrifuge to collect liquid.

steps.title: Run Repair and A‑Tailing Thermocycler
steps.instruction: Program the thermocycler for: 1 hour at 37 °C, then 10 min at 65 °C, then hold at 4 °C.

steps.title: Add SMRTbell Cleanup Beads (95 µL)
steps.instruction: Add 95 µL of resuspended, room‑temperature SMRTbell cleanup beads to each sample.

steps.title: Prepare Ligation Mix (RM2)
steps.instruction: In a new tube combine the following (adjusted for the number of libraries plus 10 % overage, or 25 % if ≥8 libraries): SMRTbell adapter (4 µL per library, only for non‑barcoded samples), Ligation mix (30 µL per library), and Ligation enhancer (1 µL per library). This yields 35 µL per non‑barcoded library or 31 µL per barcoded library.

steps.title: Add RM2 to Samples and Mix
steps.instruction: Add the appropriate volume of RM2 to each sample (31 µL for barcoded, 35 µL for non‑barcoded), bringing the total volume to 95 µL, pipette‑mix with wide‑bore tips, and quick‑spin the strip.

steps.title: Run Adapter Ligation Thermocycler
steps.instruction: Run the adapter ligation program on the thermocycler as specified in the SMRTbell 3.0 manual.

steps.title: Post‑Ligation Bead Cleanup
steps.instruction: Perform bead‑based purification of the ligated library.

substeps.instruction: Using wide‑bore tips, pipette‑mix the beads until evenly distributed.
Quick‑spin the strip, then let stand at room temperature for 10 min to allow DNA binding.
Place the strip in a magnetic separation rack until beads are fully separated.
Carefully remove and discard the cleared supernatant.
Add 200 µL (or enough to cover the beads) of freshly prepared 80 % ethanol, wait 30 s, then discard the ethanol. Repeat this ethanol wash once more.
Remove residual ethanol by quick‑spinning, returning the strip to the magnetic rack, and pipetting off any remaining ethanol.
Immediately add 40 µL of elution buffer, resuspend the beads by pipetting, and incubate at room temperature for 5 min.
Place the strip back on the magnetic rack, transfer the cleared supernatant (the purified library) to a new tube strip, and discard the beads.

steps.title: Prepare Nuclease Master Mix (RM3)
steps.instruction: In a new tube combine Nuclease buffer (5 µL per library) and Nuclease mix (5 µL per library) for a total of 10 µL per library, then increase the volume by 10 % (or 25 % if preparing eight or more libraries).

steps.title: Add RM3 to Samples and Mix
steps.instruction: Add 10 µL of the prepared RM3 to each sample (final volume 50 µL), pipette‑mix with wide‑bore tips, and quick‑spin the strip.

steps.title: Run Nuclease Treatment Thermocycler
steps.instruction: Run the nuclease treatment program on the thermocycler as described in the manual.

steps.title: Post‑Nuclease Bead Cleanup
steps.instruction: Purify the nuclease‑treated library using magnetic beads.

substeps.instruction: Using wide‑bore tips, pipette‑mix the beads until evenly distributed.
Quick‑spin the strip and let stand at room temperature for 10 min for DNA binding.
Place the strip in a magnetic rack until beads separate fully.
Slowly remove the cleared supernatant (optionally save it).
Add 200 µL (or enough to cover the beads) of freshly prepared 80 % ethanol, wait 30 s, discard ethanol. Repeat the ethanol wash once.
Remove residual ethanol by quick‑spinning, returning to the magnetic rack, and pipetting off any remaining ethanol.
Immediately add 15 µL of elution buffer, resuspend beads by pipetting 10 times or until evenly distributed, then quick‑spin.
Incubate at room temperature for 5 min to elute DNA.
Place the strip on the magnetic rack, transfer the cleared supernatant to a new tube strip, and discard the beads.

steps.title: Quantify Library DNA with Qubit
steps.instruction: Measure DNA concentration of each library using a Qubit fluorometer with the 1× dsDNA HS kit and calculate total mass.

steps.title: Store Libraries at Appropriate Temperature
steps.instruction: Store SMRTbell libraries at 4 °C if sequencing within one week; for long‑term storage keep at –20 °C and minimize freeze‑thaw cycles.

steps.title: Complete Multiplexing Calculator Spreadsheet
steps.instruction: Open Express Microbial Multiplexing Calculator.xlsm, optionally enter sample IDs, input expected genome size (bases) for each sample, enable macros if prompted, press Calculate (cell D3), enter desired total pool volume in cell C6 (minimum 100 µL), add each library’s Qubit concentration to the ‘Optional Sample Conc (ng/µL)’ column, and add average shear size (bases) from Femto Pulse QC to the ‘Avg Shear Size (bases)’ column.

steps.title: Dilute Library 1:10 for Qubit
steps.instruction: Dilute 1 µL of each library with 9 µL of elution buffer, mixing with a wide‑bore tip.

steps.title: Quantify Diluted Library and Calculate Concentration
steps.instruction: Measure the diluted library with the Qubit 1× dsDNA High Sensitivity kit and calculate the actual library concentration by multiplying the Qubit reading by 10.

steps.title: Dilute to 250 pg/µL and Measure Size
steps.instruction: Further dilute the 1:10 library dilution to 250 pg/µL using Femto Pulse dilution buffer, then assess final SMRTbell library size distribution on a Femto Pulse system (required for non‑multiplexed libraries, optional for multiplexed pools).

steps.title: Pool Libraries into Lo‑Bind Tube
steps.instruction: Pool the calculated volumes (µL) for each sample into a 1.5 mL DNA Lo‑Bind tube.

steps.title: Quantify Pooled Library with Qubit
steps.instruction: Measure the concentration of the pooled library using the Qubit 1× dsDNA HS kit.

steps.title: Concentrate Under‑Concentrated Pools (Bead Cleanup)
steps.instruction: If the pool is under‑concentrated, perform a 1× SMRTbell bead cleanup:

substeps.instruction: Add an equal volume of SMRTbell cleanup beads (1 × v/v) to the pool.
Mix beads with a wide‑bore tip until evenly distributed, quick‑spin, and let stand at room temperature for 10 min.
Place the tube in a magnetic rack, remove and discard supernatant.
Wash beads twice with 200 µL 80 % ethanol (30 s each wash).
Remove residual ethanol by quick‑spinning and discarding remaining liquid.
Add 20 µL elution buffer, resuspend beads by pipetting 10 times, incubate at room temperature for 5 min.
Place tube on magnetic rack, transfer cleared supernatant (concentrated library) to a new tube, discard beads.

steps.title: Dilute Over‑Concentrated Pools After Size Check
steps.instruction: If the pool is over‑concentrated, first confirm library size with Femto Pulse; then dilute the pool to the appropriate concentration (20–60 ng/µL for ≥10 kb libraries or 6–20 ng/µL for <10 kb libraries) using the calculated dilution factor.

steps.title: Final Library Storage
steps.instruction: Store the final SMRTbell libraries at 4 °C if sequencing within one week, otherwise at –20 °C, minimizing freeze‑thaw cycles.

steps.title: Load Libraries onto Sequel IIe
steps.instruction: Proceed to load the SMRTbell 3.0 libraries onto the Sequel IIe system according to the instrument’s loading protocol.
